transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Ah... come, sit near the warm stone. Tell me, child of the valley, what does the air smell like above now, after the sun has passed?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't care about the air. My name is Salim and my brother Omar was taken down here because of me. I need to find him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Salim. A good name, still warm on the tongue. Does the Sidr tree still stand by the eastern path, or has the heat finally bent it low?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The tree is still there. But that doesn't help me. Please, just tell me how to find my brother.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Still standing. Good. Some things remember better than I do. Tell me — after the rains, does the valley smell of wet dust or sweet leaves?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It smells like mud and wet stone. Why do you keep asking me this when Omar is alone in the dark somewhere?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Mud and stone. Yes, that was always the valley's true scent. And the call to prayer from the old mosque — does it still echo clean off the ridge?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes, it echoes clean. Now you answer me — do you know where they took him or not?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Still clean. Good. Does your mother still bake bread at dawn, or has the hour shifted with the seasons?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Don't talk about my mother. I can't go back to her without Omar. Please stop asking about the village.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I remember that fear. Sharp and bright as morning. What food do they share at night, when the work is done and voices grow soft?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Rice and lamb. But I am not here to talk about dinner. You know this place. Tell me who took him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Rice and lamb. Yes, that was for nights when the world still felt held together. Does the rain still come sudden from the mountains, or does it warn you now?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It comes sudden and loud, just like always. Now you answer me — how do I get my brother back?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Sudden rain. The valley still has a temper then. Tell me, does the wadi still sing after the rare rain, or has it gone quiet like the rest of us?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Why do you keep doing this? Every time I ask something real, you ask me about the valley. Are you going to help me or not?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I am talking to you, am I not? That is more than the dark has offered me in forty years. Now — do the goats still sleep near the old walls at night?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes, the goats still sleep by the walls. I will answer every question you have if you just tell me something useful.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Every question. That is a generous offer. Tell me then — when the evening comes, does the wind still carry salt from the far sea into Hadramout?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Sometimes it does, when the season is right. Please, I am answering everything. Now help me find him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Sometimes. Yes. The sea remembers its children even from far away. Tell me one more thing — at the market at dusk, does it still smell of coffee and cardamom?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes, coffee and cardamom, always. Old man, I have answered everything. Now it is your turn.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You are stalling me now. Sharp eyes for someone so young. Yes. I know who rules this dark. And I have the words that could help you face him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then give them to me. Please. Omar is alone because of me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I am not giving them to you. Your brother is somewhere in the dark. And you are here, with me. That is enough for now.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How can you say that? He is a child and he is scared and it is my fault he is there.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I have waited forty years with only stone and echoes. I will not trade this hour for anything. Not even your need.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You are choosing your loneliness over my brother's life. Do you understand that?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Yes. I am. Sit or go, Salim. But the prayer stays with me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You are a cruel man.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I am a lonely one. There is a difference.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I cannot stay here while he is down there. I am going.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will come back, Hanash. I swear I will come back for that prayer.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Promises fall lightly down here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: This one won't.
